title: Ravindra and Chapman Ruled Out of New Zealand's ODI Series Against India
excerpt: A hamstring that needs two more weeks and a shoulder injured in a promo shoot leave the hosts without two first-choice batters for all five ODIs against India, starting Wednesday in Auckland.
body:
• New Zealand have ruled Rachin Ravindra and Mark Chapman out of the entire five-match ODI series against India, which opens at Eden Park, Auckland, on Wednesday, November 4.
  • Chapman's left hamstring needs two more weeks of rehabilitation after an MRI scan; Ravindra's right shoulder has not recovered enough for him to field at full capacity.
  • Tim Seifert will now stay for the full series, Henry Nicholls joins for the first three ODIs, and Dean Foxcroft comes in for the last two.
  • For India fans: the hosts lose two of their most productive white-ball batters days after India took the T20I series 3-2, reshaping the contest before a ball is bowled.

New Zealand will begin their five-match ODI series against India on Wednesday without two of their first-choice batters, after Rachin Ravindra and Mark Chapman were ruled out of the full series on the eve of the squad's assembly in Auckland.

An MRI scan showed that Chapman's left hamstring requires another two weeks of rehabilitation, according to ESPNcricinfo. Ravindra's right shoulder, injured during a promotional shoot in September, has not recovered to the point where he can field comfortably. Chapman suffered his hamstring tear at the European T20 Premier League, also in September.

"Everyone knows what an asset Mark and Rachin are to this side so it's a shame they have to miss this series. With Rachin, his shoulder hasn't quite recovered to a position where he could field comfortably in white-ball cricket, so with the Test series later this month we don't want to take any undue risks."

— Rob Walter, New Zealand head coach

How the squad reshapes

Tim Seifert, originally named only for the fourth and fifth ODIs, will now remain with the squad for the entire series. Henry Nicholls has been recalled for the first three matches — a timely return, after he made 119 opening the batting for Canterbury in the Ford Trophy on Saturday. Nicholls has played 92 ODIs and was part of New Zealand's tour of the West Indies in July. Dean Foxcroft replaces him for the final two games.

There is movement in the bowling group as well. Matt Henry, who was ruled out midway through the T20I series against India, joined the ODI squad on Monday and his readiness to play will be assessed. Matthew Fisher, originally picked only for the last two games, stays for the full series as an additional bowling option.

What it means for the series

India arrive for the ODIs having won the T20I series 3-2, and the hosts' batting order now has two significant holes. Ravindra and Chapman were central to New Zealand's white-ball plans, and their absence pushes more responsibility onto Devon Conway, Daryl Mitchell and Glenn Phillips in the middle order.

India have injury business of their own to manage: as we reported earlier, Prasidh Krishna has been ruled out of the ODI series as he works back from a hamstring injury. The series is part of a long tour that also includes two Tests later this month — one reason New Zealand are unwilling to rush Ravindra's shoulder with red-ball cricket ahead.

The first ODI is at Eden Park in Auckland on Wednesday, November 4, with the squad assembling on Monday.
